title: Enhanced PVDF Membranes with Modified Silica Nanoparticles for Direct Contact Membrane Distillation
summary: This paper investigates the development of polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) membranes modified with superhydrophobic silica nanoparticles for direct contact membrane distillation (DCMD). The study utilizes a vapor-induced phase separation (VIPS) process to prepare the membranes, focusing on improving their hydrophobicity and resistance to wetting. Key findings indicate that the addition of functionalized nanoparticles significantly increases the water contact angle and liquid entry pressure, achieving superhydrophobic properties. While higher nanoparticle loading slightly reduces water flux due to decreased pore size, it substantially enhances salt rejection and overall DCMD performance, making these membranes competitive for desalination applications.
